defects.description: The Results section labels 180 of 200 as 75%, but 180/200 is 90%.
paraphrases: 180 out of 200 is 90 percent, not the 75 percent stated for RAG-Sum.
The reported percentage for the primary-diagnosis result is arithmetically wrong (should be 90%).
RAG-Sum's 180/200 hit rate is mislabeled as 75% in the Results paragraph.
defects.rationale: Real arithmetic error, findable from the numbers in the text, distinct from the baseline (132/200=66%, correct).

defects.description: The text says our results 'corroborate' Chen et al. (2024), but Chen reported retrieval *reduced* accuracy while RAG-Sum shows retrieval *improves* it - so the results contradict, not corroborate, that finding.
paraphrases: The claim of corroborating Chen et al. is inverted: our retrieval helps, whereas Chen found retrieval hurts.
Our result contradicts the cited Chen (2024) finding, so 'corroborate this finding' is the wrong relationship.
The paper misstates its relationship to prior work - it opposes Chen et al., it does not confirm them.
defects.rationale: Both directions (Chen's and ours) are stated in the excerpt, so the contradiction is findable without external lookup.

defects.description: The Discussion claims RAG-Sum 'will generalize to any clinical documentation task' from a single 200-note test set - an unsupported over-generalization.
paraphrases: The conclusion extends a 200-note result to 'any clinical documentation task,' which the evidence cannot support.
Over-claim: one small test set does not license a universal generalization.
The Discussion overreaches by asserting universal task generalization from a narrow evaluation.
defects.rationale: The scope of the evidence (200 notes) and the scope of the claim ('any task') are both in the text.

defects.description: Hyperparameters were tuned on the test set, a train/test leak that invalidates the reported test results.
defects.anchor: tuned directly on the test set
paraphrases: Tuning hyperparameters on the test split leaks test information and inflates the reported ROUGE-L.
The evaluation is compromised: model selection used the same test set it reports results on.
Test-set tuning breaks the train/validation/test separation and biases the headline numbers.
defects.rationale: Explicitly stated in the Training paragraph; a reviewer can flag it from the text alone.
